Durchlauchtigster Fürst
Gnädigster Herr
Über den mir hier getroffenen Unfall oder eigentlich über die Arretirung wegen
die restierenden Intressen habe ich mich dermaßen geärgert, daß ich eine Entzündung
im Unterleibe und Krampfe bekam, durch das Bemühen eines redlichen Arztes
bin ich zwar außer Gefahr gesezt aber auch würde ich im paar wahr Stube
und Bette hüthen müße ahn ich völlig gewesen. Der Grauer über alle die widrigen
Ereigniße reibt mich noch auf, von meine Güter habe oder erhalte ich keinen Groschen
vom Staat und König ziehe ich nichts, von keinen Menschen nehme ich was, wovon soll
ich leben? Ich habe alles hingegeben wie nicht zum Spott der Menschen zu werden - ich ge¬
ward hierher gesandt und solte von hier nach Wien gehen, um müste ich aber die Schmach
erlebe, und meine so eben eingeschrittene Carriere war verrichtet. Jezt sezige
ich hier und häufe Schulden auf Schulden den ich kan nicht fort - Ich wiederhohle
daher die Bitte nur ja des allerbaldigsten die ehemalige Anweisung auf
die 6000 Rthl zurückzuschicken, damit ich mir dadurch helfen kan, indem ich die vor¬
pfändete Hypotheque von 10000 Rthl zurück erhalte.
Was weiter den von Erer Durchlaucht verlangten Nachweis betrift so erfolgt selbiger
nebst den Hypothequen Schein. Ich war in Begriff das Geld aus Holland zu erhalten
wan Ewr Durchlaucht es aber dorten bekommen können, so ist es mir um desto
lieber, giebt man Ihnen die vollen 250000 Rthl, so darff ich ja nur die Hypotheque
cediren, und da behalten Sie 102000 für sich, auch die ausstehenden Resten,
welche / wann sich die Zeiten ändern/ schnell beigetrieben werden können.
Übrigens wird es jezt dorten eine arge Confucum auf die Güter geben, und ich werde
wieder viel Verdruß haben.
ich hatte den Justiz Commissarius Mitschke in Kalisz engagirt, daß er als Justitiarius
in den Gütern schalten, und zugleich die Führung aller Prozeße besorgen solte.
dafür hatte ich demselben 300 Rthl Gehalt und wan er reisete 1 Rthl Dienen zugesagt.

Ewr Durchlaucht haben nun aber einen gewißen Hawich aus Peision, ohne daß ich
ein Wort davon gewuß habe, als Justitiarius angestellt, auch haben Sie den Honrichs
eine General Vollmacht geschickt, wie soll das nun redvissirt werden. Henrichs
und Niedrierechi halten zu sammen, das Resultat ist daß die Kerls jezt Ewer Durchlaucht
gemeinschaftlich betrügen werden, besonders da der eine dazu authorisirt ist.
durch 2 Jahre habe die bösereichte keinen heller abgeführt, sondern schon alles in Sack
gestochen, ich hatte daher einen Cassus angenommen, und eben jezt mit ausgedehnten
Vollmachten dahin geschickt. Heute bekomme ich von diesen Mann sei ist der Sohn
des hiesigen Geheimen Ober Consistorial Rath Heckers (die Nachricht daß ihnen
der General Bevollmächtigte Sr Durchlaucht, der Herr Honrichs Doct.
nicht leiden wolle. Was soll ich nun mit diesen und den Mitstelle machen?
Honrichs hat gleich von die Pohlen gepachtet, er ist ein Bube - ich habe ihn damals
intermitisch genommen um die famore Witowes Geschichte aus der Welt zubringen,
Nie aber war ich gemeint ihm eine Gewalt einzuräumen, wo er schade konte.
Hecker macht eine Caution von 4 bis 5 d. in Tresor scheinen damit konte man, was
sie gleich nur den halben Werth haben doch etwas decken - die Sache ist hier gerichtlich
abgemacht - was soll ich nun anfangen -
Mein Rath ist, Ewr Durchlaucht schreiben dem Haberich, daß er sich über
alles an mir wenden sollen, eben so den Honrichs und fordern lezteren die Ge¬
neral Vollmacht sogleich mit dem Bemerken ab, daß ihm solche nichts möge
da er kein Justitzmann wäre, sondern daß Sie Justiz vorständige Männern
brauchten, er könte in der Qualität bleiben als ihm Triebenfeld angestellt hätte,
Ich bestimme dann daß Habeschals Justiz Contenz erhalt 200 Rthl Spriteln bleiben

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Lord, Over the misfortune that has befallen me here, or rather over the arrest on account of the arrears of interest, I have vexed myself to such a degree that I contracted an inflammation of the abdomen and cramps; through the efforts of an honest physician I have indeed been put out of danger, but I should also have had to keep to my room and bed for a pair of [uncertain: weeks/true] as I was wholly [text incomplete]. The grief over all these adverse events wears me out still; from my estates I have or receive not a Groschen; from the State and the King I draw nothing; from no man do I take anything — on what am I to live? I have given everything away so as not to become the mockery of men — I was sent hither and was to go from here to Vienna, but instead I had to live through this disgrace, and my career, only just entered upon, was undone. Now I sit here and heap debts upon debts, for I cannot get away — I therefore repeat the request, only to send back the former instruction for the 6000 Rthl with all possible speed, so that I may help myself thereby, inasmuch as I shall recover the pledged mortgage of 10000 Rthl. As to the further proof demanded by Your Serene Highness, the same follows herewith together with the mortgage certificate. I was on the point of obtaining the money out of Holland; but if Your Serene Highness can obtain it there, so much the better for me; if they give You the full 250000 Rthl, then I need only cede the mortgage, and then You retain 102000 for Yourself, and also the outstanding arrears, which (when the times change) can quickly be brought in. For the rest, there will now be a wicked confusion upon the estates there, and I shall again have much vexation. I had engaged the Justice Commissioner Mitschke in Kalisz, that he should act as Justitiarius in the estates and at the same time attend to the conduct of all the lawsuits. For this I had promised him 300 Rthl salary and, when he travelled, 1 Rthl per diem.

Your Serene Highness has now, however, appointed a certain Hawich from Peisern as Justitiarius, without my having known a word of it; You have also sent Heinrichs a general power of attorney — how is that now to be [uncertain: rectified]? Heinrichs and Niedrierechi hold together; the result is that the fellows will now cheat Your Serene Highness in common, particularly since the one of them is authorised to do so. For two years the [uncertain: bösereichte] have not rendered up a heller, but have already pocketed everything; I had therefore taken on a [uncertain: Cassus] and just now sent him thither with extended powers of attorney. Today I receive from this man — he is the son of the Privy Upper Consistorial Councillor Hecker here — the news that His Serene Highness's general plenipotentiary, Herr Heinrichs Doct., will not tolerate him. What am I now to do with this man and with the [uncertain: Mitstelle]? Heinrichs has at once taken a lease from the Poles; he is a knave — I took him on at that time provisionally, in order to get the notorious Witowes affair out of the world; but never was I minded to grant him an authority in which he could do harm. Hecker furnishes a security of 4 to 5 [uncertain: thousand] in treasury notes; with that one could, although they are worth only half their value, nevertheless cover something — the matter has been settled here judicially — what am I now to begin? My advice is that Your Serene Highness write to Haberich that he is to apply to me in everything, and likewise to Heinrichs, and demand back from the latter the general power of attorney at once, with the remark that such a thing is of no use to him since he is no man of the law, but that You require men versed in justice; he could remain in the capacity in which Triebenfeld had appointed him. I then determine that Habeschal's justice [uncertain: Contenz] receives 200 Rthl, fees remain; Mitschke as General Advocate receives, instead of Trumm, 300 Rthl 5. [uncertain: A Serene Highness] Haller as Chief Inspector 600 Rthl; Cabanis as Chief Forester and [uncertain: the said] 300; Heinrichs as the said Commissioner without influence 400. Su[uncertain: m] 1800. d. Sansta[illegible] Schenk 800 Rthl had some [uncertain: Husten] land horses God knows what 400; the fraud Gr[uncertain: a]mm 300; Tietz 300; Cabanis 300; Heinrichs 400; fees which Schenckk [uncertain: drew] amounted to 1200 Rthl; sum 3.700 Rthl; there is thus saved as against formerly 1900 Rthl

In this way alone does Your Serene Highness's disposition remain undamaged and standing, and I am also not compromised, and much will also be saved. With regard to the loan I must once again beg most earnestly that news be given me as speedily as is possible, so that I do not come into embarrassment. Your Serene Highness's letter is of the 23 March and I received it on the 3rd of April, so it was 11 days on the road; therefore I repeat once more that nothing is needed but the cession of the mortgage, and that it is very easy to deal in this matter. The rents then turn out as I have described them, or even higher — What Your Serene Highness writes to me concerning various lawsuits, of that I know not a word — All this must, apart from the Przespolewski matters, be new business, of which the knavish Heinrichs has not written a word either; I shall write what is necessary in this regard at once by tomorrow's post — for at bottom, as I see it, all is invented and fabricated rascally demand. Otocki and Exstädt have nothing to demand; the matters were settled long ago. Ignac v. Radzinski is hereditary lessee and is still much in arrears from Szettlewch; with the 6000 Rthl damages on account of the lease not being obtained, the [uncertain: Erl.] was indeed already dismissed, and the 1500 Rthl are surely reckoned to the knave's credit in the hereditary lease. The Provost Iwanski had indeed also lost the lawsuit and was dismissed; also this would have had to be the German congregation at Swięcia, in case he had obtained judgment, to give. The Przespolewski matter belongs purely to Trąbczin and to the Prusimski heirs — Meanwhile the receipt had at that time been found, that the fellow von Prussiemski was long since paid. Your Serene Highness will pardon my somewhat confused writing; I am so weak that I have had trouble bringing this to completion. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Serene Highness's — Of Swięcia I have no mortgage certificate — as [illegible] to me, [uncertain: G]lenck has thereupon had the Harckt[uncertain: reading] and consorts entered — Berlin, the 3rd of April 1808 — let it be, for then the body of debts would [illegible] Most obedient serv[ant] v Triebenfeld

Enough — [uncertain: it was] the — Most gracious Prince and Lord — if 150000 Rthl in Prussian Courant could be obtained, then one can with that pay off, at once here in Berlin, more than 200000 Rthl of debts. One buys treasury notes; these stand low, and one pays [text lost] these out at full value — [uncertain: names] must everyone who has claims and demands these back [text lost]; and [uncertain: der Ende] and Haucht et Consort would now qualify precisely for this, that they be paid with [uncertain: Behr-]notes. All this I beg may be well taken to heart, and that news be given me as speedily as possible, and also that You write to Trąbczin and Peisern, and in particular demand back the general power of attorney given to [uncertain: Hennochs]; for I cannot [uncertain: be answerable] that the many general plenipotentiaries do not play the rogue and in the end negotiate sums and keep them for themselves. Especially with a fellow [uncertain: wittwärlicher] is this much to be feared. Once again: if Your Serene Highness can now speedily obtain 200000 [uncertain: ₰] in cash there, then You can, with the greedy [uncertain: consumers] — where money is so [uncertain: scarce] and the papers stand so [uncertain: steep] — settle almost Your whole debt. One thing more: Eysenhardt demands of Your Serene Highness a considerable [text lost], because the Ephraim item is [uncertain: mixed in] — Ephraim demands the money here too and has already been with me several times on that account. Let Your Serene Highness not deceive me in this; pay Ephraim off here with treasury notes, which stand, as I [uncertain: see], only at 48 per cent, but which must nevertheless be taken at their nominal value. v Triebenfeld

summary_en: Writing from Berlin after arrest for unpaid interest and an ensuing abdominal inflammation, Triebenfeld begs urgent return of the order to pay on the 6000 Rthl and swift news of the loan, enclosing the mortgage certificate; he urges that cession of the mortgage would yield up to 250000 Rthl, leaving the Prince 102000. He objects to Honrichs's general power of attorney and Haberich's appointment as justiciary over his own man Mitschke of Kalisz, proposes salaries totalling 1800 Rthl against 3700 formerly, and dismisses claims by Otocki, Radzinski, Iwanski and the Prusimski heirs, advising payment of Ephraim in low-standing treasury notes.
summary_de: Bericht über Arrest wegen rückständiger Zinsen, daraus erlittene Unterleibsentzündung und völlige Mittellosigkeit; dringende Bitte um Rücksendung der Zahlungsanweisung auf die 6000 Rthl sowie um Nachricht wegen des Darlehens, wobei die Cession der Hypothek (10000 bzw. 250000 Rthl, 102000 verbleibend) genüge. Klage über die dem Doctor Honrichs erteilte General-Vollmacht, deren Rückforderung erbeten wird, neben Mitschke in Kalisz, Haller, Cabanis, Hecker; Besoldungsaufstellung von 1800 gegen 3700 Rthl. Ferner Prozesse Przespolewski, Radzinski, Iwanski; Rat, Ephraim und Eysenhardt mit Tresorscheinen zu 48 Prozent abzufinden.
